nodes.description: Pelvic endometriosis commonly coexists with catamenial pneumothorax but is not a prerequisite. Its detection depends on the extent of gynecologic assessment. Coexistence is compatible with a pelvic migration hypothesis but does not establish the origin of every thoracic lesion.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Catamenial Pneumothorax: A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: The presence of pelvic endometriosis was reported in only 55% of patients with catamenial pneumothorax.

nodes.description: Air entering the pleural space through any of the proposed routes collapses the lung, producing the pneumothorax and its symptoms.

evidence.snippet: recurrent accumulation of air in the pleural cavity in reproductive-age women without concomitant respiratory diseases

nodes.description: Alveolar rupture is the proposed distal injury in the prostaglandin account of CP. The hormonal-to-rupture chain remains hypothetical and need not apply to endometriotic or transdiaphragmatic cases.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial pneumothorax - a review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: High concentration of prostaglandin F2 during menses may cause blood vessels and bronchioles to contract, which leads to alveolar rupture and development of pneumothorax.

nodes.description: Bronchiolar smooth-muscle contraction is one proposed consequence of elevated menstrual prostaglandin F2alpha. Its contribution to alveolar rupture in CP remains hypothetical.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial pneumothorax - a review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: High concentration of prostaglandin F2 during menses may cause blood vessels and bronchioles to contract, which leads to alveolar rupture and development of pneumothorax.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Catamenial Pneumothorax: A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: Diagnosis was mostly made clinically, with the patients complaining of the typical symptoms of shortness of breath and recurrent chest pain or shoulder pain a day before to 72 hours after menses.

nodes.description: Acute supportive management of the pneumothorax by tube thoracostomy to re-expand the collapsed lung, distinct from the causal therapies that prevent recurrence.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial Pneumothorax-Still an Unveiled Disease.
evidence.snippet: in some cases, a chest tube insertion may be necessary to allow for re-expansion of the lung tissue

nodes.description: Local differentiation of thoracic coelomic or mesothelial cells into endometrial-like tissue has been proposed as an alternative to transported uterine cells. Direct demonstration of this origin in catamenial pneumothorax is lacking.

evidence.reference_title: The Importance of Stromal Endometriosis in Thoracic Endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: The coelomic metaplasia theory suggests that endometriosis arises by metaplasia of coelomic epithelial cells.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial Pneumothorax as the First Expression of Thoracic Endometriosis Syndrome and Pelvic Endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: All patients presented with symptoms including chest pain, cough, shortness of breath, and hemothorax.

nodes.description: Repeated proliferation and breakdown of thoracic endometrial implants during menstruation is proposed to cause local bleeding and injury. Histological invasion is observed, but the entire temporal sequence has not been experimentally established in CP.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial pneumothorax - a review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: The cyclical proliferation and necrosis of endometrial cells may injure the diaphragm, enabling the cells to migrate further into the chest and the visceral pleura, which may lead to pulmonary alveolar injury and pneumothorax.

nodes.description: Thoracic endometriotic tissue commonly expresses estrogen and progesterone receptors. This supports hormonal responsiveness and the rationale for suppressing cyclic implant activity; receptor staining alone does not prove that ovarian hormones establish the implants.

evidence.reference_title: Dynamics of thoracic endometriosis in the pleural cavity.
evidence.snippet: All endometriotic stromal tissues were stained positive for ER, PgR, and CD10, and all endometriotic gland tissues were stained positive for ER and PgR, but negative for CD10.

nodes.description: Diaphragmatic defects are observed during CP surgery. They provide a possible communication between peritoneal and pleural spaces. Endometriotic injury is one proposed origin; the observation of a defect alone does not demonstrate genital-tract air passage.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial pneumothorax.
evidence.snippet: At video-assisted thoracic surgery, diaphragmatic defects and nodules are the most frequent findings.

nodes.description: Identified diaphragmatic defects or involved tissue may be treated by suture, plication, resection or mesh reinforcement as part of a combined surgical plan. A small retrospective CP cohort associated diaphragm resection with fewer recurrences; this is not randomized evidence that all patients require resection.

evidence.reference_title: Recurrence-Free Survival after Postoperative Hormone Therapy for Catamenial Pneumothorax.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of risk factors for postoperative recurrence identified diaphragm resection as a protective factor against recurrence (hazard ratio, 0.16; 95% confidence interval, 0.03–0.77; p=0.022)

evidence.reference_title: Surgical management of catamenial pneumothorax: a systematic review.
evidence.snippet: Diaphragmatic interventions included primary suture repair, resection of affected diaphragm, and mesh coverage or reinforcement.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Catamenial Pneumothorax: A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: Diagnosis was mostly made clinically, with the patients complaining of the typical symptoms of shortness of breath and recurrent chest pain or shoulder pain a day before to 72 hours after menses.

nodes.description: GnRH agonists suppress ovarian cycling and are used as adjuncts around surgery to reduce implant activity. Small observational series support reduced recurrence, but comparative superiority and optimal duration remain uncertain. Menopausal symptoms and bone-density loss limit prolonged treatment; fertility goals and tolerability affect selection.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial Pneumothorax-Still an Unveiled Disease.
evidence.snippet: The use of GnRH analogs has been correlated with a lower incidence of CP recurrence than surgery alone or postoperative estrogen-progesterone therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Surgical management of catamenial pneumothorax: a systematic review.
evidence.snippet: The practical constraints of prolonged GnRH agonist use — including menopausal side effects and bone density loss — represent a genuine clinical challenge that requires individualised discussion with patients.

nodes.description: Progestins, continuous combined hormonal preparations and danazol have been used to suppress menstruation or endometrial activity. These regimens do not all produce the same degree of ovarian suppression or hypoestrogenism. Postoperative therapy is coordinated with gynecology according to recurrence risk, adverse effects and fertility preferences; available comparisons are observational.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial Pneumothorax-Still an Unveiled Disease.
evidence.snippet: Pharmacotherapy aims to suppress ovarian estrogen production and atrophy of functional endometrium (including ectopic endometrium within the chest cavity), resulting in a lack of menstruation.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial pneumothorax - a review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: The primary aim of treatment is to induce hypoestrogenism, resulting in the lack of menses.

evidence.reference_title: Postoperative hormonal therapies reduce the recurrence of thoracic endometriosis-related pneumothorax.
evidence.snippet: Likewise, the multivariable analysis revealed postoperative hormonal therapies were significantly associated with the risk reduction of recurrence (hazard ratio 0.28, P < 0.001).

evidence.reference_title: Recurrence-Free Survival after Postoperative Hormone Therapy for Catamenial Pneumothorax.
evidence.snippet: Patients who received hormone therapy exhibited a lower rate of recurrence than those who did not; however, the difference was not statistically significant, likely due to the small sample size.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial Pneumothorax-Still an Unveiled Disease.
evidence.snippet: Commonly used pharmaceutics include danazol, oral contraceptives, progesterone agents, and gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists

nodes.description: Hematogenous or lymphatic transport of endometrial cells is an alternative proposed origin of thoracic implants. Detection of circulating endometrial-like cells does not by itself demonstrate their implantation in the lung.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial pneumothorax - a review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Metastatic spread or pulmonary microembolization from endometrial cells through blood or lymph vessels.

nodes.description: First step of a proposed "physiological" theory: prostaglandin F2alpha rises to high levels during menstruation. This branch does not require endometrial implants and is offered as a complementary, non-settled account.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial Pneumothorax-Still an Unveiled Disease.
evidence.snippet: high F2 prostaglandin levels during menstruation induce vasoconstriction and bronchospasm, resulting in alveolar rupture and pneumothorax

nodes.description: Chemical or mechanical pleurodesis promotes pleural symphysis to reduce recurrent air accumulation. It is frequently combined with treatment of diaphragm defects and visible endometriotic lesions; pleurodesis alone may leave contributory lesions untreated.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial pneumothorax.
evidence.snippet: Partial diaphragmatic resection and/or exeresis of visceral pleural implants, as well as talc pleurodesis, are nowadays frequently carried out.

nodes.description: Pulmonary vasoconstriction is a separate proposed consequence of elevated menstrual prostaglandin F2alpha. The suggested link from vasospasm to alveolar injury is not established in individual CP patients.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial pneumothorax - a review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: High concentration of prostaglandin F2 during menses may cause blood vessels and bronchioles to contract, which leads to alveolar rupture and development of pneumothorax.

nodes.description: Recurrent spontaneous pneumothorax, overwhelmingly right-sided (about 93% of cases), occurring in a fixed temporal relationship to menstruation.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Catamenial Pneumothorax: A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: Pneumothorax was found mainly in the right lung (456 of 490 cases, 93%).

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial pneumothorax.
evidence.snippet: Usually onset of lung collapse is less than 72 hours after menstruation.

nodes.description: Ectopic endometrial-like stroma, sometimes accompanied by glands, occurs on the diaphragm or pleura in the endometriosis-associated subset of catamenial pneumothorax. Stromal-only lesions can be missed without appropriate immunohistochemistry. Macroscopic nodules are not equivalent to histologically confirmed endometriosis, and tissue confirmation rates depend on selection and sampling.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial Pneumothorax as the First Expression of Thoracic Endometriosis Syndrome and Pelvic Endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: Thirteen (40.6%) women were then diagnosed with TES.

evidence.reference_title: Dynamics of thoracic endometriosis in the pleural cavity.
evidence.snippet: Endometriotic stromal cells were confirmed in all 160 (160/160: 100%) diaphragmatic lesions, and endometriotic gland cells were found in 61 (61/160: 38%).

nodes.description: VATS permits systematic inspection and selective resection of thoracic endometriotic lesions, including small visceral pleural cystic lesions, and assessment of diaphragm defects. Procedures are combined according to operative findings; evidence does not establish a single universally optimal surgical technique.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial pneumothorax.
evidence.snippet: Partial diaphragmatic resection and/or exeresis of visceral pleural implants, as well as talc pleurodesis, are nowadays frequently carried out.

evidence.reference_title: Dynamics of thoracic endometriosis in the pleural cavity.
evidence.snippet: Because rupture of cystic lesions causes TERP, careful inspection of the visceral pleura is important in order to avoid overlooking small cystic lesions.

nodes.description: A proposed, non-mutually-exclusive route in which air passes from the peritoneal cavity — which communicates with the genital tract during menstruation when the cervical mucus plug is shed — through diaphragmatic fenestrations into the pleural space.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial pneumothorax.
evidence.snippet: Findings of surgical explorations support the theory of transabdominal-transdiaphragmatic passage of air to explain the pathogenesis of catamenial pneumothorax.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial Pneumothorax-Still an Unveiled Disease.
evidence.snippet: The passage of air from the uterus via the diaphragmatic fenestrations into the pleural cavity results in the development of pneumothorax.

nodes.description: Retrograde transport of menstrual endometrial tissue through the fallopian tubes and peritoneal cavity toward the diaphragm is a proposed route of thoracic seeding. Passage through diaphragmatic defects and subsequent implantation remain a mechanistic interpretation rather than a demonstrated route in every patient.

evidence.reference_title: Catamenial pneumothorax - a review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Endometrial cells may migrate from the uterus, through the fallopian tubes, into the lesser pelvis and further, into the area of the diaphragm.

nodes.description: A proposed local route of air leakage through lung-surface defects associated with breakdown of visceral pleural endometriotic lesions. This route is distinct from air crossing the diaphragm.

evidence.reference_title: Dynamics of thoracic endometriosis in the pleural cavity.
evidence.snippet: it is hypothesized that air enters the intrathoracic space through a lung surface defect caused by the deciduation of endometriotic lesions in the visceral pleura during menstruation

nodes.description: In histologically confirmed thoracic endometriosis-related pneumothorax, endometriotic tissue can extend inward from the visceral pleural surface through elastic layers. This observation supports a local tissue-injury route in endometriosis-associated CP; it is not evidence that every CP case has invasive implants.

evidence.reference_title: Dynamics of thoracic endometriosis in the pleural cavity.
evidence.snippet: Some endometriotic tissues stayed on visceral pleural surfaces, while others demonstrated inward tissue invasion from the visceral pleural surfaces
